core_assessment:
Independently read every selected context and proof range74-112,170-280,286-613,650-1142,1185-1427 before viewing the selector difficulty reason. The property-P proof passes from a finite translation-stable field extension to a finite map of smooth curves. A finite branch locus invariant under a nontorsion translation is empty; Riemann-Hurwitz and the elliptic morphism classification reduce the extension to a sublattice cover. Its normality then identifies the embedded extension inside the union K. Tsen supplies C1 for the directed union, not the nontrivial no-finite-translation-extension conclusion.
The Riccati classification is verified by the actual gauge matrices and their antidiagonal equations. In the scalar case the ratio sigma(u)/u is a phi-coboundary. Its norm is phi-invariant and hence constant, so a constant root normalizes it to norm1 and Hilbert90 supplies m. The resulting scalar coefficient descends; the remaining finite cyclic constant matrix representation diagonalizes, giving two invariant row ratios. The two-step descent first uses M_(kLambda)/M_(Z+k tau Z), and if necessary obtains three tau-translates, scalarizes over that intermediate field, and descends again. Distinctness is maintained by invertibility of the matrices.
The theta-gcd construction removes the common shifted numerator/denominator factor r. Substitution into the Riccati equation and the two coprimeness conditions force divisor bounds p<=p2 and q<=phi^-1(p3). Quasiperiodicity then forces equal degrees and the weight relation weight(p/q)=deg(r)h modulo kLambda. The corrected /k multiplier is actually printed at1126 and1134, so the operative proof uses the correct formula despite550.
For irreducibility, the lifted zero/pole support of b on C/(2Lambda) restricts weight(p/q) to ell z0-deg(q)h modulo Lambda, with |ell|<=4. The stronger author group-intersection condition excludes nonzero multiples of h in these cosets, forcing deg(r)=deg(q)=deg(p)=0 and hence a constant Riccati solution, incompatible with nonconstant b.
For imprimitivity the second Riccati equation uses phi^2. The support bounds allow extra negative h shifts in the numerator and positive h shifts in the denominator; any such mass contributes a positive integer d to(2deg(r)+d)h=ell z0 modulo Lambda, with |ell|<=8. Nonresonance removes all these extra contributions and then deg(r). At each lattice pole the bracket is holomorphic, so u must have the full double pole there; equality of total degrees forces exactly the zero divisor of b as well. Thus u=cb. The pole at -2h forces c=-1/a, and the remaining equality is1=0. This is a separate argument, not a repetition of the first Riccati conclusion.
The determinant sentence is an abbreviated standard first-order PV/divisor check, assessed below. For the arithmetic step, wp(z0) algebraic implies the elliptic point and its integer multiples are algebraic. A relation m1 h=m2 z0+lambda either makes m1 h a period, forcing m1=0 by nontorsion, or gives an elliptic logarithm of a nonzero algebraic point; Schneider makes that logarithm transcendental, contrary to algebraic h and integer m1. This establishes the stronger group-intersection condition already explicitly stated by the author.

On a period cover containing f, the divisor of phi(f)/f has sum0 on every h-orbit, by finite-support telescoping. Its orbit sum is therefore -2m, contradiction. Hence the determinant image is infinite and thus G_m.
